newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian securities tax plan may fall - Livshits.
newsitem.headline: Russian securities tax plan may fall - Livshits.

text.p: Proposals for a 15 percent tax on Russian government securities transactions may not make it through parliament, Interfax news agency quoted Finance Minister Alexander Livshits as saying on Tuesday.

"We understand there are quite a few opponents of this proposal in the State Duma (lower house of parliament), and I do not rule out the possibility that deputies will not pass this draft law," Livshits said.
He said the ministry, which introduced the draft into parliament as a way to increase budget revenues, does not expect much from it.
Central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said last week the proposed tax would not be applied retroactively.
He said the bank would oppose the tax and that, if it were levied, it would only lead to a rise in the yield necessary to raise the necessary resources for the government.
